events.summary: 4th Annual 20s & 30s Trail Work Weekend in AMC’s Maine Woods

location.title:
75 Little Lyford Pond Rd
Greenville, ME

description.plain:
Friday, August 7, 2026 | 5:00 PM
https://activities.outdoors.org/s/oc-activity/a5UVX000001BgY12AK/
Join the Worcester and Boston Chapter 20s & 30s groups for a weekend of trail work in the beautiful and remote Maine Woods! This three night, three day trip includes two full days of trail work and three nights' stay at AMC's Little Lyford Lodge, plus a hike/exploration day on Monday. Participants are encouraged to arrive by late afternoon/early evening Friday to provide ample time to get to the lodge for dinner before the gate closes.This trip is designed for people in their 20s & 30s who are interested in learning about trail work and bringing back newly gained skills to local chapter opportunities. No trail work experience is required, only a desire to learn trail work techniques and contribute to the restoration of mountain trails. Activities may include revitalizing trails, repairing benches and bridges, and building check steps and will be somewhat tailored to the interests and abilities of the group. The trail work will involve hiking a few miles each day with moderate elevation gain. We will be working under the leadership and guidance of AMC’s Professional Trail Crew with tools and safety gear provided. Expect to be out for about 6-7 hours Saturday and 6-7 hours Sunday.At the end of each day, we’ll enjoy social time and dinner back at the lodge. Enjoy the dark sky (New England’s only certified International Dark Sky Park!), the Perseid meteor shower, paddling on the pond, swimming in the Pleasant River, and campfires in the evening. Canoes and kayaks are free with our stay. Accommodations are cabins and a bunkhouse at Little Lyford, one of AMC's lodges in the heart of the 100-mile Wilderness in the Maine Woods. Breakfast, trail lunch, and dinner (Saturday breakfast through Monday breakfast) are included with the cost of the stay. The cost for the 3 night trip is $345. Once you register for the activity here, the leaders will send a separate screening form. Once participants have registered and have been confirmed, a leader will reach out with the required information for payment.Cancellation policy: Participants must notify trip leaders as soon as possible if they can no longer participate. A refund will be issued ONLY IF leaders can fill your spot.

events.summary: Flags on the 48 - A September 11 Memorial Hike: South Kinsman

description.plain:
Saturday, September 12, 2026
https://activities.outdoors.org/s/oc-activity/a5UVX000001FKlp2AG/
We are organizing a team for the Flags on the 48 memorial event. Join our Chapter in honoring those who died on Sept 11 by helping to raise our flag over South Kinsman. Out and back hike via the Lonesome Lake, Fishin' Jimmy and Mt. Kinsman trails, 10 mi., ~ 3,200' elevation gain, with average, strenuous, and very strenuous terrain, at a slower-moderate pace (1-2 mph). Limited to 12, including the leaders, physically fit hikers with current, i.e., within the past year, upcountry hiking experience. All participants will be screened for this hike to ensure we can stay together as a group; otherwise, it can create an unsafe situation.This is a full day event with an early start. Leave room in your pack to carry group gear: flag, PVC pipe used to construct the flagpole, guy lines and other hardware for securing the pole. We will arrive at the peak to allow time to set up/secure the flagpole at the summit and raise the flag before 12 noon. The flag then flies from noon through 2 pm. We then will lower the flag, deconstruct the flag pole,guy lines, etc. and pack up our gear.Required gear:• Bring what you need to stay warm, dry, and happy for an extended day on the summit• A pack large enough to hold all your gear + group gear• 3-4 liters of water• Snacks and trail lunch• Pad to sit on• Sunscreen• Bug repellent• Headlamp• Rain gear• Layers to add & subtract to regulate your body temperature throughout the day, including, and not limited to, a puffy jacket, winter hat/mittens/gloves

Friday, October 9, 2026 | 12:00 PM
https://activities.outdoors.org/s/oc-activity/a5UVX000001D6F72AK/
 You are cordially invited to join the Worcester Chapter for our 33rd anniversary trip to Western Maine to enjoy the gorgeous autumn colors of Maine over Columbus Day weekend. We'll be staying at the Maine House, located on the shore of beautiful Lake Christopher in the village of Bryant Pond. The charming historic house will be the base for our many hikes and other outdoor activities. The Maine House has cozy private rooms for couples and comfy bunks for singles. The dining area has a panoramic view over the lake, and a large living room with a fireplace invites all to relax and socialize during the evening. In addition, there is a hot tub and a steam room to help you recover after your day of activities. Paddle right out the door on Lake Christopher in canoes provided by the house. The trip fee includes three nights lodging (Fri - Sun), three breakfasts and make-your-own-lunch buffets, and two tasty dinners. Everyone helps with set-up or clean-up for a meal. With about 30 people on the trip, we will be able to offer various levels of hikes each day, ranging from easy to strenuous, as well as other activities. We will lead one road biking trip, and there are nearby DIY paddling opportunities. The trip cost this year is $175. Join us for this Worcester Chapter classic which draws participants from all over the club.
